bet.text: Shooting would dominate high-level play, so the climber ranked lower, and a 360 degree turret was planned to shoot from anywhere on the field.

demand.text: Scoring cargo first. The team wanted to traverse from the start, but lower on its list. Before the championship it theorized that a traversal climb would be of little use to a team shooting to the end, and it brought both a traversal and a high-rung option.

auto.text: In the first Einstein final it scored two, then picked up a blue cargo and rolled it under the red hangar side.

cycle.text: A wide intake clamps bouncing balls from a halfway preset. Two sensed chambers hold one ball each; a wrong color is ejected by the shooter at low speed. Hood and wheel speeds follow the robot's position, and the turret leads when it moves.
A recap counts about 23, 25 and 19 cargo in the Einstein finals.

endgame.text: Two telescoping tubes on gas shocks pivot outside the frame to the next rung; the gyro tells when the swing is steadier. Traversal in about five seconds.
A poster times one climb at eight seconds from entering the hangar.
It missed traversal in its one round-robin loss.
At Ventura, a post says, it used L3 climbs.

fallback.text: A prototype high-rung climber, with a passive arm swung out by surgical tubing as the elevator lifts, takes about three seconds. It came to the championship as an alternative.

gave_up.text: The turret's cable chain is a lot of weight and space and took several printed versions. The team was on the fence about 2x2 rails until inset MK4i modules gave back the lost inch.
The outer frame may not be a weight-efficient way to hold a turret, but saved it from countless faceplants.
A post reports a fall at Ventura.

changed.text: Intake: pneumatic four-bar with 3 in flex wheels, then 4 in, then chain and sprocket, then a wrapped roller. Hood: linear servos, then a Falcon, for speed and range. The Limelight moved to the top.
Accelerator wheels did more harm than good and went before the third event to save weight.
The climber reached a third version; a team machinist counts at least four iterations of the whole robot.

outcome.text: 68-8-1 in official play; won the Turing division; pick 1 of the Turing alliance on Einstein; championship finalist; ranked 22 by championship OPR (55.95, Turing).
